newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate approves Brady buyback bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate approves Brady buyback bill.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate approved a bill authorizing the central bank to buy back Brady bonds and swap them for other sovereign paper, an official said.
In a show of hands, the Senate approved the measure which places no limit on the total value of operations but sets strict Senate oversight terms.
The bill allows the central bank to restructure all of its $57 billion in Brady bonds should it desire to do so.
The bank must report to the Senate 30 days after each operation or within 10 working days if operations total $500 million or more cumulatively.
Failure by the central bank to report on time will mean automatic suspension of authority to carry out further buybacks or debt swaps.
The bank will also have to satisfy senators it has made a "profit" either by reducing its external debt stocklpile, increasing the maturity or improving the profile of external debt.
Average prices of Brazilian Bradies over the six months before an operation will serve as a yardstick to determine minimum return, the bill said.

The central bank will have the authority to contract national or international institutions to lead manage the deals, with their fees partly based on gains in terms of price, interest rates and maturity of the new debt.
If the bank fails to convince senators it has made a profit, authorization for buybacks and debt swaps will be automatically suspended.
If the Senate does not respond to central bank reports on operations within 10 days, authority to carry out further operations is automatically granted to the bank.
The bill also stipulates that any net gains made through such operations must be used to reduce the internal or external debt stock.
